_comment: KILL example. Negative ablation Sharpe delta, high PBO, miscalibrated engine.

output.reasoning: The bias engine lost 0.21 Sharpe compared to making no decisions at all — it is actively worse than random. The calibration Brier score (0.29) is poor, meaning the engine's confidence numbers are unreliable. The hysteresis rate is 51%, which means the router is oscillating almost every other decision rather than holding a position long enough to matter. All three signals point the same direction: the engine is adding noise, not signal.
output.evidence_summary: 68 days, 287 decisions — adequate sample. Calibration Brier: 0.29 (poor — engine's confidence is not meaningful). Sharpe delta: -0.21 (the engine hurt performance relative to making no call at all). PBO: 0.67 (high overfitting risk — even the bad result may not be a stable bad result). Hysteresis rate: 51% (router is flip-flopping constantly). Conclusion: the bias engine in its current form is not helping. Kill it (flip BIAS_ENGINE_MODE back to OFF), and diagnose the feature snapshot quality or HMM state design before re-attempting SHADOW mode.
